provenance.note: Nineteen title/sentence pairs are owner-authored reference lines. MAY 12 and AUG 19 are needs-review date-specific repair lines for Production-only selected events. Dates and attributions remain calculation-owned.

winter-current.title: Give the idea structure
winter-current.sentence: Put a schedule, limit, cost, or deadline around the part you are ready to build.

winter-current.title: Follow the better idea
winter-current.sentence: Pay attention to the possibility that gives the work more meaning or a more interesting direction, then give it somewhere practical to go.

winter-current.title: A responsibility reaches its limit
winter-current.sentence: A move, repair, living arrangement, family duty, or household obligation may need a decision.

spring.title: The old setup changes
spring.sentence: A role, schedule, relationship, or agreement may need different terms because you or your circumstances have changed.

spring.title: Read the terms carefully
spring.sentence: A request or opportunity may give someone else more control over the terms.

spring.title: Make the method easier to keep
spring.sentence: Try a different tool, schedule, or process where it can make the writing easier to continue.

spring.title: Try the other method
spring.sentence: Give the different tool, schedule, or format a real test before deciding which route works better.

spring.title: Build around your actual week
spring.sentence: Choose the practice or limit you can keep before the next Saturn pass.

summer.title: A longer conversation begins
summer.sentence: Give one idea enough room to become something you can keep developing.

summer.title: Put the important part into words
summer.sentence: An announcement, application, or piece of writing may need a clear answer from someone else.

summer.title: Say what you are doing clearly
summer.sentence: Send the message, explain the work, or accept the introduction while it is easier to be understood clearly.

summer.title: The calendar tells the truth
summer.sentence: Notice which basic routines and relationships lose time every time another commitment gets added.

summer.title: Private words reach a wider audience
summer.sentence: Review what you wrote for yourself before it becomes something other people need to understand.

summer.title: Home and work compete for time
summer.sentence: Decide how much of the week each one can realistically receive.

autumn.title: Put the idea into working order
autumn.sentence: Turn what has been developing into a draft, schedule, process, or plan you can keep working with.

autumn.title: Test it against a real week
autumn.sentence: Keep the part of the May structure that still works and change the part that does not.

autumn.title: Test the new format
autumn.sentence: Ask what the change improves before you discard a format that still works.

autumn.title: State the terms, round 1
autumn.sentence: What you want may conflict with somebody else's plan.

winter-next.title: Terms, round 2
winter-next.sentence: Say what would actually resolve the disagreement from October, including what each person can realistically commit to.

winter-next.title: The career question gets concrete
winter-next.sentence: An application, title, project, client, publication, or professional decision may reach a point where somebody needs to answer.

winter-next.title: Keep what survived the year
winter-next.sentence: The practice that still works after May and October is the one worth carrying forward.
